identity.title: Are inner disc misalignments common? ALMA reveals an isotropic outer disc inclination distribution for young dipper stars
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: The ALMA data used to resolve the dipper discs in our sample come from both our targeted ALMA programme as well as archival ALMA programmes
Thus we uniformly (re)derive the inclinations of 24 dipper discs resolved with (sub-)mm interferometry from ALMA.

targets.name: 24 K2/C2 dippers in rho Ophiuchi (12) and Upper Scorpius (12)

question.value: Are the outer-disc inclinations of dipper stars (resolved by ALMA) concentrated near edge-on, as the accretion-warp picture predicts, or isotropically distributed, implying inner-disc misalignments?

evidence.quote: In this work, we uniformly (re)analyze resolved (sub-)mm ALMA data for two dozen dipper discs in an effort to robustly infer the distribution of their outer disc inclinations.
The identification of a face-on dipper disc and growing evidence of inner disc misalignments brings this scenario into question.

referee_caveats_inferred: Gaussian-disc inclinations of marginally resolved sources may be biased high or poorly constrained; only four DSHARP sources were used to validate
Posterior sampling for the isotropy test does not propagate the multi-modal inclination posteriors the authors admit emcee handles poorly
Selection of 'resolved' discs is itself a function of inclination and size, which could bias the distribution
The 0.26 cutoff in cos(i) is chosen from the observed deficit rather than independently motivated
Small sample (24, three flagged binaries) limits statistical power of the KS test; a non-rejection does not prove isotropy

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Tens of GB (calibrated measurement sets for about nine projects, 24 targets); fits need GPU or many CPU cores
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA projects are listed but the fitting priors, per-source data choices and per-source results are not given in the text, and no code is stated as released; the isotropy test is describable but not exactly reproducible.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public data stated only indirectly, and the visibility-model recipe lacks priors and parametrisation, so results could not be redone to match the paper's numbers.
